title: Agent Skills: Portable Contract and Runtime Boundary
service: SkillPack: the lesson's SKILL.md toolchain for a host: the YAML-subset parser and name rules, a writer that YAML hosts read the same way, an ordered package validator, a streaming TAP check of the host's lifecycle events, and the workflow edges between skills with an install order

deviations: Part 1 has five planted bugs instead of the four suggested. The added one, line_content keeping the \r of \r\n, gives the far-from-root error the spec asks for: parse_frontmatter says 'SKILL.md must begin with an exact --- line' about a file whose first line is ---.

Part 1's overfix guards are not the suggested splitlines/U+2028 check. str.splitlines and CRLF-exact content are already traps in lessons 01, 03, 07, 09 and 14 of this chapter, and the spec allows a trap kind at most twice per chapter. The guards here are the indentation strip() removes, a closing --- that is the file's last line, the body starting right after a ---\r\n line, and the lesson's name rules (2fa-helper, two hyphens). splitlines(keepends=True) passes and is a follow-up question; a CRLF body is only checked to start after the closing line.

Part 1 times a 2.6 MB SKILL.md with 50,000 body lines rather than 500 KB. On this machine the slicing version takes about 0.1 s at 500 KB (copying cache-resident text is fast), which leaves no room for 8x margins on both sides; 2.6 MB gives 1.0-1.9 s against a 0.1 s limit and about 5 ms for the fix.
parse_frontmatter keeps the body exactly as written (the lesson's code strips it) so that Part 2 can round-trip it; body-required tests body.strip().

Part 2's quoting rules add YAML-typed scalars (numbers, dates, booleans, null) for core fields and metadata, from the lesson's own SKILL.md (lesson: "22"); runtime extension fields stay host-typed (user-invocable: false). The suggested 'a body line starting with --- must not end the frontmatter' is a regression check (a --- rule in the body) rather than a writer trap, because this grammar never makes the writer emit an unindented --- line.

Part 3's allowed-tools-shape also covers tools separated by tabs or line breaks (a | block of names), reading the lesson's 'non-empty space-separated string' literally; the lesson's code only checks that it is non-empty.

Part 4 adds an explicit 'ended' event, which the lesson's eight stages do not name, to close a session; a failed validation followed by nothing is ok (the host did its job), and sessions still open at the end get a line with their first problem or 'session not ended'.

Part 5: a reference is 'invoke the `name` skill' with the name in backticks, a guard ('if that skill is unavailable') covers the nearest reference before it, and a missing dependency does not hold a skill back from the install order, since skills are invoked through the runtime rather than imported.
